sentences.text: Offences complained of : Secs.498A, 504, 506 of IPC Opinion of the Judge : Accused found not guilty.
(GIRISH CHATNI)
XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT
The P.S.I., of H.A.L., Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable under sections Secs.498A, 504, 506 of IPC.

C.C.No.61319/2024 2. BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :
It is the case of the complainant that, she got married with accused on 02.03.2008 as per Hindu rites and customs at Sri.Lakshmi Venkateshwara Kalyana Mantapa at Srinivasapura and out of wedlock they have got two children.
It is further alleged that, the accused used to consume alcohol on daily basis and picked up quarrel with CW.1 and subjected her to cruelty by harassing her both physically and mentally.

It is further alleged that, the accused harassed the CW.1 by demanding the money to buy alcohol and abused her in filthy language, accused asked her to give divorce, if she refused to give money and also threatened her with dire consequences.
Based on the typed complaint lodged by C.W.1, CW.07 has registered the case against accused in P.S. Crime No.737/2023 for the offence punishable under sections 498A, 504, 506 of IPC.
Investigating Officer/ CW.07 after completion of the investigation has submitted final report against the accused for the above said offences.
3. During the crime stage, the accused appeared before this court and enlarged on bail.
Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above mentioned offence C.C.No.61319/2024 alleged against the accused and registered the criminal case against him.
After registering the case, copies of the final report and it's enclosures were furnished to him in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charges.
Hence, charges framed and read over to the accused.
He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

4. In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined one witness out of 07 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 and relied upon documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.08 and closed its side.

In lieu of absence of incriminating circumstances appearing against accused,
recording of his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.

Perused the materials on record.
Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused has abused CW.1 in filthy language and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.504 of IPC ?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused has threatened CW.1 with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.506 of IPC ?
4. What Order?

7. My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point Nos.1 to 3 : In the Negative.
 Point No.4 : As per the final order  for the following;
 REASONS  8. POINT Nos.1 to 3 :-
As these three points are interlinked, I have taken up these points together for common discussion to avoid repeti- tion of facts & evidence.
C.C.No.61319/2024
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined the complainant/victim/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and relied upon eight documents.

9. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined the complainant /
victim CW.1 as PW.1, wherein, the said witness has not supported the case of the prosecution.

The learned APP appearing for the State with permission treated the said witness as hostile and fully cross examined her, wherein, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW.1 in order to prove the guilt of the accused.

10. On perusal of the materials on record and the oral & documentary evidence of P.W.1, she has categorically admitted that, she has compromised the matter with the accused and she is leading happy marital life with accused.

In view of the evidence of P.W.1, since the matter was compromised, the prayer of the learned Senior Asst. Public Prosecutor for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses was rejected as no purpose would be served.

As the P.W.1 has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution, the evidence on record is not at all helpful to substantiate the State By Hal Ps vs Manjunath K on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86492232/
3 guilt of the accused.

sentences.text: Hence, there is no cogent and convincing evidence against the accused.

Accordingly, the benefit of doubt has to C.C.No.61319/2024 be extended to the accused and hence,
the Point Nos.1 to 3 are answered in the "Negative".
11. Point No.4

: - In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is acquitted of the offence punishable under Secs.498A, 504, 506 of IPC.
The Bail bond and surety bond of the accused shall be in force for the period of 6 months and thereafter it shall be cancelled without further orders.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and typed by her, corrected by me and then signed and pronounced in the Open Court on this date the 09 th day of May, 2025.)
